note: Level extras A1 wrote the five A1 cases; A2 extras added the dative card and the A2 uses (plural, about / after, interests, where with przed, za, nad, pod). The vocative comes with B1 (spec 08 §4).

cases.name: Mianownik
cases.summary: The dictionary form: the subject of the sentence, and the noun after to jest / to są.

uses.label: Plural: men vs everyone and everything else
uses.pl: Moi koledzy są mili, a te książki są nowe.
uses.en: My colleagues are nice, and these books are new.

traps: After być a noun goes into the instrumental: Jestem studentem, not Jestem student. With to jest the noun stays in the nominative: To jest student.
Masculine personal plurals change the last consonant: student → studenci, Polak → Polacy. Not studenty, Polaki.
A group with at least one man takes the masculine personal forms: Ania i Tomek są zmęczeni. Animals and children do not: Psy są głodne, Dzieci są małe.

contrasts.rule: The subject is in the nominative. The direct object is in the accusative: feminine nouns change -a to -ę.

cases.name: Dopełniacz
cases.summary: Absence, possession, quantity, and after many prepositions.

uses.label: After do, z, bez, dla, u
Plural after dużo, kilka, ile? and 5+
uses.en: There were a lot of people at the concert.

uses.label: Next to, opposite, near
uses.en: The post office is next to the bank.

traps: English does not change the object after not, so learners keep the accusative: Nie mam czas ✗ → Nie mam czasu ✓.
Masculine people and animals that end in a consonant always take -a (brata, kota). For things it is -a or -u, and you learn them in pairs (dom – domu, chleb – chleba).
After nie only an object that would be in the accusative changes. The subject stays in the nominative (Kawa nie jest droga), and other cases stay too (Nie pomagam mamie).
After dużo, kilka, ile? and 5+ the noun is genitive plural and the verb is singular: Było dużo ludzi, not Były dużo ludzie.
Feminine and neuter nouns usually lose their last vowel, often with an e added: minuta → minut, piwo → piw, książka → książek. Not książków.

contrasts.rule: A positive sentence takes the accusative. The same sentence with nie takes the genitive.
do + genitive = where to (a shop, a city). w + locative = where you are.

cases.name: Celownik
cases.summary: The person who receives something, after pomagać and dziękować, and the person in podoba mi się and jest mi zimno.

uses.label: podobać się: the person who likes it

singular.masculine: -owi (Tomkowi, lekarzowi); -u on a short list: bratu, panu, ojcu, kotu, psu
singular.feminine: -e with a softened consonant (mamie, siostrze, córce); -i / -y after soft consonants (Ani, babci, pracy)

traps: English says "to Mum"; Polish has no preposition here: Daję prezent do mamy ✗ → Daję mamie prezent ✓. do means "to a place".
pomagać and dziękować take the dative, not the accusative: Pomagam brata ✗ → Pomagam bratu ✓, Dziękuję pana ✗ → Dziękuję panu ✓.
With podobać się the thing you like is the subject and you are in the dative: Ja podobam ten film ✗ → Ten film mi się podoba ✓.
How you feel is jest + dative + an adverb: Jestem zimny ✗ → Jest mi zimno ✓.

contrasts.rule: The thing you give or buy is the accusative; the person who gets it is the dative.
Feminine nouns look the same in the dative and the locative: only the question differs (komu? / o kim?).

cases.name: Biernik
cases.summary: The direct object: the person or thing the action goes to.

uses.label: Plural objects: men take -ów / -y / -i, the rest = nominative
uses.en: I know these students. I like cats.

uses.label: How long, and for what: na
uses.en: I'd like a room for three nights. (a woman speaking)

prepositions: na (how long, what for: na trzy noce, coś na kaszel, ochota na)

traps: English marks the object only by its place in the sentence. Polish needs the ending: Lubię kawę, not Lubię kawa.
Masculine people and animals take -a, like the genitive: Mam brata, Mam psa. Things do not change: Mam dom.
After nie the object switches to the genitive: Mam czas. → Nie mam czasu.
Going into a building or a town takes do + genitive, not w + accusative: Idę do szkoły, not Idę w szkołę.
In the plural only men change: Znam te studenty ✗ → Znam tych studentów ✓. Animals are like things: Lubię psy, not Lubię psów.

contrasts.rule: Positive sentence: accusative. Negated sentence: genitive.
A feminine noun ends in -a as the subject and in -ę as the object.
na + accusative = where to. na + locative = where. With w, where to is usually do + genitive: Idę do szkoły, Jestem w szkole.

cases.name: Narzędnik
cases.summary: Who or what someone is after być, the company you are in after z (with), and how you travel or pay.

uses.label: A job or nationality after być
Means of transport
uses.en: I'm going to work by bus.

uses.label: Together with people, in the plural
Where: przed, za, nad, pod, między
uses.en: The cat is sleeping under the bed.

uses.label: Jobs in the plural, after być

verbs: być + noun (a job, a nationality, a role)

traps: English uses the same form in "I am a student" and "the student is here". Polish needs the instrumental after być: Jestem student ✗ → Jestem studentem ✓.
An adjective alone after być stays in the nominative: Jestem zmęczony, not Jestem zmęczonym. A first name in an introduction stays in the nominative too: Jestem Tomek.
After to jest the noun stays in the nominative: To jest student. But: On jest studentem.
"By bus" has no preposition: Jadę z autobusem ✗ → Jadę autobusem ✓. z autobusem means "together with a bus".
"Interested in" is one verb with się, not a copy of English: Jestem zainteresowany w historii ✗ → Interesuję się historią ✓.
The plural ending is -ami for almost every noun: z kolegami, z koleżankami. Learn the few in -mi: z ludźmi, z dziećmi, z przyjaciółmi.

contrasts.rule: to jest + nominative names someone; być + noun says what someone is and takes the instrumental.
z meaning with takes the instrumental; z meaning from takes the genitive.

cases.name: Miejscownik
cases.summary: Where someone or something is, after w and na. The locative never stands alone: it always follows a preposition.

uses.label: Surfaces, after na
uses.en: The phone is on the table.

uses.label: At home
uses.en: In the evening I'm at home.

uses.label: About: o
uses.en: We're talking about the new film.

uses.label: After: po
uses.en: After work I'm going to the gym.

uses.label: Months, this / next / last …
uses.en: I have an exam next week.

verbs: rozmawiać o, mówić o, myśleć o, pamiętać o

singular.masculine: -e with a softened consonant (Kraków → w Krakowie); -u after k, g, ch and soft consonants (w banku, w hotelu), and in w domu
singular.feminine: -e with a softened consonant (w szkole, w Polsce); -i / -y after soft consonants (w kuchni, w pracy)
singular.neuter: -e with a softened consonant (w kinie); -u after k, g, ch (na lotnisku, w łóżku) and after soft consonants (w mieszkaniu); -um does not change (w muzeum)

traps: In English the noun after in or at never changes. In Polish it does: Mieszkam w Kraków ✗ → Mieszkam w Krakowie ✓.
Before -e the consonant softens: k → c (w Polsce), g → dz (w Pradze), t → ci (na poczcie), d → dzi (w ogrodzie), r → rz (w biurze), ł → l (w szkole).
dom takes -u: w domu, not w domie.
Some places take na, not w: na poczcie, na dworcu, na przystanku, na rynku, na lotnisku, na uniwersytecie.
The locative says where you are, not where you go: Idę w sklepie ✗ → Idę do sklepu ✓.
"About" after rozmawiać, mówić, myśleć takes the locative: Rozmawiamy o pracę ✗ → Rozmawiamy o pracy ✓. (o + accusative is for asking: pytać o drogę.)
The locative plural is -ach, the instrumental plural -ami: w sklepach, but z kolegami.

contrasts.rule: w + locative = where you are; do + genitive = where you go.
na + locative = where you are; na + accusative = where you go.
